scope: Theorem 6.1 (Projected moments of a deterministic row likelihood) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 55. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each fixed real r and each ε > 0, there is d0 = d0(r, ε) such that, for every fixed d ≥ d0 and every deterministic mask M, outside a disorder event of probability tending to zero there is a set Bn,d,M satisfying µ(Bn,d,M ) ≤ e−cn , max i Ex [︁ (AM i,x(Xd))r]︁ ≤ eεd + on(1) (x / ∈ Bn,d,M ). (6.2) Here c > 0 can depend on the fixed d, r, ε, but the estimates in the proof are uniform in the deterministic mask. Thus the notation eor(d) for these moments always means dimension first and then d → ∞. For 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 the upper bound 1 follows directly from Jensen’s inequality. Negative r in Equation (6.2) refers to the unrestricted positive likelihood, not to a likelihood multiplied by a cutoff indicator. The theorem also holds in its integrated form: if M = Mα ranges over a deterministic measurable family with a finite measure on its parameter space, the good disorder event can be chosen so that the integrated Gibbs mass of the exceptional starts is exponentially small. This includes masks determined by simplex times in a fixed finite path expansion and the independent Poisson schedules used below. It does not assert a simultaneous bound for a mask selected to maximize an error after seeing the disorder.
